$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under src/ imports this file.
purpose: The mutation ledger for WIN-302's three acceptance clauses, run against
`src/composition/context-factories.test.ts` and the suites that share its
subject. One entry per mutation, carrying the file (repository-relative), the
EXACT text removed or changed (`from`), what replaced it (`to`), and the NAMED
cases that were SEEN to go red (`kills`).
CLAUSE 1 -- every context's contract factory resolves from apps/core-api,
proved by import. M09 renames a `.`-route factory in the artifact the runner
resolves; M04-M06 remove a subpath-route entry point and M11-M12 a `.` one.
CLAUSE 2 -- a mutation removing ONE entry point turns a NAMED test red, on
BOTH routes. M04, M05 and M06 each delete one `./application/index.js`; M11
and M12 each delete one `.`. Each turns that context's own case red while
the unrelated per-context cases stay green. They cover the import situations
the tree has: `channels` and `memory` are imported by nothing but their
factory-entries module; `tenancy` is also imported statically by
`app.module.ts`; `governance` and `providers` are also imported statically
by `context-ports.ts`. For those three, `installation.test.ts` fails at LOAD,
as it did before this tranche, which is why the per-context cases live in a
file that imports neither module at its top. M12 also reddens `conversations`,
whose package loads `providers` at run time.
CLAUSE 3 -- no stale count survives, and a readback stops the next one. M01
and M02 put the pre-WIN-302 figure back into the prose of the two files the
WIN-302 comment names. M03 moves the constant and leaves the prose alone. M08
restores both files exactly as they stood at the branch base 3f422333, which
is the state the readback exists to have caught. M13-M18 are the shapes the
first readback could not see, four of them the round-1 verifier's probes.
ROUND 2. The first version of this sweep had ten entries, all on the subpath
route or the prose. The round-1 verifier showed that removing a `.` entry
failed the whole file at load, because the seven `.`-route cases imported the
package literally, and that four stale phrasings passed the readback. Every
entry below was re-run on the tree that fixes both, and M11-M21 are new.
A SEPARATE FILE FROM `mutations-win267-g3.json`, which recorded the partition
this tranche replaced. Its kill names for G3-M05..G3-M09 name a case that no
longer exists, and that ledger's `retiredKills` says where each property is
held now, rather than rewriting what was measured at ff06655f.
procedure: Base: tejas/m2m4-lane-factories, the tree of the commit that carries this file
(branched from tejas/m2-m4-complete @ 3f422333).
suite    pnpm --filter @platos/core-api exec vitest run \
src/composition/context-factories.test.ts \
src/composition/installation.test.ts
baseline 50 passed (50): 20 in context-factories.test.ts, 30 in
installation.test.ts. Re-confirmed green after the sweep.
Each mutation was applied to the working tree from a byte copy, the suite run,
and the copy restored. `git status` showed the tree unchanged after each.
M09 edits `dist/`, which is gitignored, and was restored the same way. M10 and
M19 also ran `node --test scripts/arch/gen-v1-skeleton.test.mjs` (baseline 26
passed).
WHY NO ENTRY IS A MODULE-LOAD FAILURE OF THE FILE UNDER TEST. A literal
`await import("@platos/context-channels/application/index.js")` inside a case
fails in Vite's import-analysis TRANSFORM when the manifest does not publish
the subpath (vitest 3.1.4, vite 5.4.21: `Missing "./application/index.js"
specifier`, `Tests  no tests`), and a literal `await import("@platos/context-memory")`
fails the same way when the manifest does not publish `.`. Both are vacuous
reds. Through a relative module that re-exports the factory, the same removal
fails ONE case and passes its siblings, which is the shape `factory-entries/`
implements for all seventeen contexts.
